newsitem.title: USA: Brown and Williamson argues against award.
newsitem.headline: Brown and Williamson argues against award.

text.p: Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, said its attorneys urged a Florida judge on Tuesday to set aside a jury award of $750,000 to a smoker with lung cancer.
The company said in a statement its lawyers argued that "prejudicial errors made during the July cigarette product liability trial should cause the verdict to be overturned."

In the case of Grady Carter, of Orange Park, Fla, a jury in Jacksonville ruled in August that Brown and Williamson was negligent and made a dangerous and defective product He smoked for 50 years until he was diagnosed with lung cancer.
"We are absolutely convinced that the Carter verdict will be overturned," said attorney Tom Bezanson.
Among other things the company argued:

-- "The jury was allowed to hear speculative, self-serving testimony from Mr. Carter about what he would have done had there been additional warnings about the health risks associated with cigarettes."
-- "The judge allowed plantiff's experts to broadly speculate in their testimony, unfairly prejudicing the jury."
-- "Contrary to the rules of evidence, the judge permitted submission of documents that had no relevance to the trial."

-- "The judge allowed speculative testimony that American Tobacco could and should have produced a 'safer cigarette' without any extrinsic evidence of a feasible alternative design and how it would have made a difference, as is required by law."
